questions.question: The calendar for the year 2017 will be the same as which of the following years?
questions.solution:
The standard rules for calendar repetition are:

1. If the year is a leap year + 1, it repeats after 6 years.

2. If the year is a leap year + 2, it repeats after 11 years.

3. If the year is a leap year + 3, it repeats after 11 years.

4. If the year is a leap year, it repeats after 28 years.

__Calculation:__

The given year is 2017.

First, we determine the type of year. We divide the year by 4 to check for leap years:

The year 2016 is a leap year (divisible by 4).

Thus, 2017 = 2016 + 1 (i.e., it is a Leap year + 1).

According to the rule, a Leap year + 1 repeats after 6 years.

Repetition Year = 2017 + 6 = 2023.

Since both 2017 and 2023 are ordinary years, they have identical calendars.

Hence, the correct answer is “**Option 2**”.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

We can verify the year by counting odd days until the sum is divisible by 7 (Note: an ordinary year has 1 odd day and a leap year has 2 odd days):

O dd days in 2017 = 1

Odd days in 2018 = 1

Odd days in 2019 = 1

Odd days in 2020 = 2 (Leap year)

Odd days in 2021 = 1

Odd days in 2022 = 1

Total sum of odd days = 1 + 1 + 1 + 2 + 1 + 1 = 7.

Since the total sum of odd days is 7 (which is a multiple of 7), the next year 2023 will start on the same day as 2017. Because both are ordinary years, the entire calendar will be the same.

Hence, the correct answer is 2023.

questions.question: How much time (in minutes) (approximately) after 2:00 PM will it take for the minute and hour hands of the clock to be at an angle of 90 degrees?
questions.solution:
At **2:00 PM**, the **minute hand** is at the 12 o clock position (0°), and the **hour hand** is at the 2 o clock position.

The angle covered by the **hour hand** at 2:00 = 2 × 30° = 60°.

For the hands to be at an angle of **90 degrees**, the **minute hand** must first cover the initial 60° gap to catch up with the **hour hand** and then move an additional 90° ahead of it.

Total relative angular distance to be covered = 60° + 90° = 150°.

Time taken = Distance ÷ Relative speed

Time = 150 ÷ 5.5 ≈ 27.27 minutes.

Rounding to the nearest whole number, the time taken is approximately **27 minutes**.

Hence, the correct answer is “**Option 1**”. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

The angle between the **hour hand** and **minute hand** is given by the formula:

Angle = |60H - 11M| over 2

Where **H** = hours and **M** = minutes.

Given **H = 2** and **Angle = 90°**:

90 = |60 times 2 - 11M| over 2

180 = |120 − 11M|

To find the time after the hands have crossed each other (since 120 − 11M = 90 would give a negative value for M):

180 = 11M − 120

11M = 180 + 120

11M = 300

M = 300 ÷ 11 ≈ 27.27 minutes.

The approximate time is **27 minutes**.

Hence, the correct answer is “**Option 1**”.

questions.question: A clock is 3 minutes slow at 9:00 AM and 7 minutes fast at 3:00 PM. At what time (in AM) will it show the correct time?
questions.solution:
Given **initial time** = **9:00 AM**

Given **final time** = **3:00 PM**

**Total time interval** from 9:00 AM to 3:00 PM = **6 hours**

Clock status at 9:00 AM = **3 minutes slow** (−3 min)

Clock status at 3:00 PM = **7 minutes fast** (+7 min)

**Total gain** in 6 hours = 7 − (−3) = **10 minutes**

The clock gains 10 minutes in 6 hours.

To show the **correct time**, the clock must gain the **initial lag** of 3 minutes.

Time taken to gain 10 minutes = 6 hours

Time taken to gain 1 minute = 6 / 10 hours

Time taken to gain 3 minutes = (6 / 10) × 3 hours

Time = 18 / 10 hours = **1.8 hours**

Converting 1.8 hours into minutes:

1.8 hours = 1 hour + 0.8 × 60 minutes

1.8 hours = 1 hour + **48 minutes**

The clock shows the correct time 1 hour and 48 minutes after 9:00 AM.

Correct time = 9:00 AM + 1 hour 48 minutes = **10:48 AM**

Hence, the correct answer is “**Option 2**”.

• The **Parliament** enacted the **Governors (Emoluments, Allowances and Privileges) Act, 1982**, to regulate these financial aspects. In 2018, the salary of the Governor was significantly increased to **3.5 lakh rupees** per month.
 
• The expenditure for the salary and allowances of the **Governor** is charged upon the **Consolidated Fund of the State**, meaning it is not subject to the vote of the state legislative assembly.
 
• If the same person is appointed as **Governor** of two or more states, the emoluments and allowances payable are allocated among the states in such proportion as the **President** may by order determine.

• The **Governor** holds office during the **pleasure of the President** as per **Article 156**, but the President does not determine the salary.
 
 
 
• **Finance Commission**:
 
 
• This is a **Constitutional Body** constituted under **Article 280** of the Constitution.
 
• Its primary function is to recommend the distribution of net proceeds of taxes between the **Union and the States** and among the states themselves.
 
 
 
• **Salary Immunity**:
 
 
• The **Constitution** ensures that the emoluments and allowances of a **Governor** cannot be diminished during his or her term of office to maintain the independence of the post.

questions.question: The Narmada River flows in which direction?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**East to West**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Narmada River** is the largest **west-flowing river** in peninsular India, traversing a distance of approximately **1,312 km**.
 
• It originates from the **Amarkantak Plateau** in the **Anuppur district** of **Madhya Pradesh** at an elevation of about 1,057 meters.
 
• The river flows through a **Rift Valley** created by down-faulting, situated between the **Vindhya Range** to the north and the **Satpura Range** to the south.
 
• Its drainage basin covers parts of **Madhya Pradesh**, **Gujarat**, **Maharashtra**, and **Chhattisgarh**, eventually emptying into the **Arabian Sea** through the **Gulf of Khambhat**.
 
• Unlike most major peninsular rivers that flow towards the east and form deltas, the Narmada flows **East to West** and forms a broad **estuary**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Geographical and Cultural Significance:**

 
 
• It is often referred to as the **Lifeline of Madhya Pradesh and Gujarat** due to its huge contribution to the state economies through irrigation and power.
 
• The **Sardar Sarovar Dam**, one of the largest water resources projects in India, is built across this river in **Gujarat**.
 
• The river creates the famous **Dhuandhar Falls** (Marble Rocks) near **Jabalpur**, where the water plunges over steep rocks.
 
• Major tributaries of the Narmada include the **Hiran**, **Orsang**, **Barna**, and **Kolar** on the right bank, and the **Sher**, **Shakkar**, **Dudhi**, and **Tawa** on the left bank.
 
• The **Tapi River** (Tapti) is the other major river in India that flows in the same **East to West** direction within a rift valley.

• Chadwick conducted an experiment where he bombarded **beryllium** with **alpha particles** emitted from a **polonium** source. This interaction produced a highly penetrating radiation that was not deflected by electric or magnetic fields.
 
• He concluded that this radiation consisted of neutral particles, which he termed **neutrons**. This discovery solved the mystery of why the **atomic mass** of most elements was higher than the combined mass of their protons and electrons.
 
• The identification of the neutron was a pivotal moment in **nuclear physics**, providing the necessary tool for the fission of **uranium-235** and leading directly to the development of the **atomic bomb**.
 
• For his significant contribution to science, **James Chadwick** was awarded the **Nobel Prize in Physics** in **1935**.

• In **1917**, he performed the first artificial transmutation of an element and is credited with the discovery of the **proton**.
 
 
 
• **Niels Bohr**:
 
 
• In **1913**, he proposed the **Bohr Model** of the atom, which integrated **quantum theory** to describe how electrons revolve in stable, circular orbits around the nucleus.
 
• He explained that electrons can only occupy specific **quantized energy levels**.
 
 
 
• **Wolfgang Pauli**:
 
 
• He was an Austrian theoretical physicist known for formulating the **Pauli Exclusion Principle** in **1925**.
 
• The principle states that no two electrons (or other **fermions**) in an atom can have the same set of four **quantum numbers**.

• In 1934, he authored the landmark book **'Planned Economy for India'**, which presented a **ten-year blueprint** for economic development and **industrialization**.

questions.question: The Industrial Licensing System was introduced in:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1951**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The industrial licensing system in India was formally established through the enactment of the **Industries (Development and Regulation) Act (IDRA)** in **1951**, which came into force in **May 1952**.
 
• The primary objective of this act was to provide the **Central Government** with the necessary powers to regulate and develop industries in accordance with national priorities and the objectives set out in the **Five-Year Plans**.
 
• Under the **1951 Act**, a license was mandatory for establishing any new industrial undertaking, manufacturing a **New Article** in an existing plant, or carrying out a substantial expansion of production capacity.
 
• The system was designed to prevent the **Concentration of Economic Power**, protect the interests of **Small-Scale Industries (SSI)**, and ensure **Balanced Regional Development** by incentivizing industries in backward areas.
 
• This regulatory framework formed the core of the **License Permit Raj**, which allowed the state to control the allocation of capital and resources to ensure they served the **Socialistic Pattern of Society**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Industrial Policy Resolution (IPR) 1948**:

 
 
• This was the first official policy statement after independence, which introduced the concept of a **Mixed Economy** where both the public and private sectors co-existed.
 
• It reserved certain sectors like **Arms and Ammunition**, **Atomic Energy**, and **Railway Transport** exclusively for the state.
 
 
 
• **Industrial Policy Resolution (IPR) 1956**:
 
 
• Often termed the **Economic Constitution of India**, it expanded the public sector's scope and classified industries into three schedules: **Schedule A** (State monopoly), **Schedule B** (State-led), and **Schedule C** (Private sector).
 
• It emphasized the development of **Heavy and Machine-building Industries** as part of the **Mahalanobis Model** of growth.
 
 
 
• **New Industrial Policy (NIP) 1991**:
 
 
• Marked by the **Liberalization, Privatization, and Globalization (LPG)** reforms, this policy abolished industrial licensing for almost all industries.
 
• Currently, compulsory licensing is limited to only five sectors, including **Defense Equipment**, **Industrial Explosives**, and **Hazardous Chemicals**, primarily for security and safety reasons.

questions.question: Which scheme provides financial incentives to promote exports from SEZs?
questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Merchandise Exports from India Scheme (MEIS)** was introduced in the **Foreign Trade Policy (FTP) 2015-20** to promote the export of notified goods produced in India.
 
• The scheme specifically includes **Special Economic Zones (SEZs)** units, making them eligible for financial rewards to offset infrastructural inefficiencies and associated costs involved in exporting.
 
• Incentives under MEIS are provided in the form of **Duty Credit Scrips**, which are calculated as a percentage (usually **2% to 7%**) of the realized **Free on Board (FOB)** value of exports in free foreign exchange.
 
• The scheme consolidated five earlier incentive programs, such as the **Focus Product Scheme (FPS)** and **Market Linked Focus Product Scheme (MLFPS)**, into a single unified framework to simplify the process for exporters.
 
• By providing these incentives, the **Ministry of Commerce and Industry** aimed to enhance the **global competitiveness** of Indian manufactured goods and increase India’s share in world trade.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Duty Credit Scrips**:

 
 
• These are **freely transferable** instruments that can be used to pay **Basic Customs Duty** on the import of inputs, capital goods, or other notified items.
 
• If an exporter cannot use the scrips for their own imports, they can be sold in the **secondary market** at a premium.
 
 
 
• **Special Economic Zones (SEZs)**:
 
 
• Governed by the **SEZ Act, 2005**, these zones are treated as **foreign territories** for trade operations and duties, offering tax holidays and simplified procedures.
 
• Units in SEZs enjoy **100% Income Tax exemption** on export income for the first 5 years under **Section 10AA** of the Income Tax Act.
 
 
 
• **Transition to RoDTEP**:
 
 
• To align with **World Trade Organization (WTO)** requirements regarding export subsidies, the MEIS was replaced by the **Remission of Duties and Taxes on Exported Products (RoDTEP)** scheme effective from **January 1, 2021**.

Telescoping Series Formula

questions.question: The perimeter of a rhombus is 100 cm. One of the diagonal is 40 cm. What is the ratio of the two diagonals?

**∴ The correct answer is 4:3.**

Formula: **Side** (a) = **Perimeter** ÷ 4; (Side)² = (d₁/2)² + (d₂/2)².

⇒ (d₂ ÷ 2)² = 625 − 400 = 225

⇒ d₂ ÷ 2 = √225 = 15 cm

⇒ **Diagonal**₂ (d₂) = 15 × 2 = 30 cm.

⇒ **Ratio** = d₁ : d₂ = 40 : 30 = 4 : 3.

**∴ The correct answer is 4:3.**

The diagonals of a **rhombus** bisect each other at **right angles** (90°) and also bisect the interior angles.

questions.question: The product of Highest Common Factor and Least Common Multiple of 2 numbers is 6930. One of the numbers is 154. What is the other number?

For any two numbers, the **product of the numbers** is equal to the **product of their HCF and LCM**.

Other number = (Product of **HCF** × **LCM**) ÷ **Given number**

Other number = 6930 ÷ 154 = 45

**∴ The correct answer is 45.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Product of **HCF** and **LCM** = 6930

One number (n₁) = 154

**Formula Used:**

n₁ × n₂ = **HCF** × **LCM**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0229b551268ee9781405d59bb8fd7a1b64ffaa045ddb3ca205e874566bf07862.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ 154 × n₂ = 6930

⇒ n₂ = 6930 ÷ 154

⇒ n₂ = 3465 ÷ 77 (Dividing by 2)

⇒ n₂ = 495 ÷ 11 (Dividing by 7)

⇒ n₂ = 45

**∴ The correct answer is 45.**

HCF and LCM Relation

For any two numbers a and b, the product of the numbers is always equal to the product of their **HCF** and **LCM**: a × b = HCF(a, b) × LCM(a, b).

Co-prime Numbers

Two numbers are said to be **co-prime** if their **Highest Common Factor (HCF)** is 1. For such numbers, their **LCM** is simply the product of the numbers.

Divisibility by HCF

The **LCM** of any set of numbers is always exactly divisible by their **HCF**.

questions.question: If A is 5 times more than B, then B is what percentage less than A?

Let **B = 1** unit.

**A** is 5 times more than B ⇒ **A = 1 + 5 = 6** units.

Difference = **6 − 1 = 5** units.

Required percentage = (5 / 6) × 100 = **83.33%**.

**∴ The correct answer is 83.33%.**

⇒ **Value of A** = 100 + 500 = **600**

⇒ **Difference** = A − B = 600 − 100 = **500**

⇒ **Percentage B is less than A** = (Difference / A) × 100

⇒ Required % = (500 / 600) × 100

⇒ Required % = 5/6 × 100 = **83.33%**

**∴ The correct answer is 83.33%.**

Difference between "Times" and "Times More"

If A is **n times B**, then A = n × B. If A is **n times more than B**, then A = B + (n × B) = (n + 1) × B.

Percentage Less = [(Higher Value − Lower Value) / Higher Value] × 100.

Marked Price and Discount

The **Selling Price** can be directly found using the formula: SP = CP × (100 + Profit%) ÷ 100.

She stiches fine dresses for the queen.

• To convert **Simple Present** into **Passive Voice**, the rule is: **Object + is/am/are + Past Participle (V3) + by + Subject**.

• The **Object** 'fine dresses' is **plural**, so the auxiliary verb **are** must be used to maintain subject-verb agreement.

• The **Past Participle** or **V3** form of the verb 'stitch' is **stitched**.

• The **Subject** pronoun 'She' is transformed into its **objective case** 'her' when placed after the preposition 'by'.

• The phrase 'for the queen' remains as an **adjunct** or secondary object in the sentence, typically following the main passive construction.

 **Additional Information__**

• Options using **were stitched** represent the **Simple Past Passive** tense. These are incorrect because the active sentence is in the **Present Tense**. The tense of the sentence must remain consistent during voice conversion.

• A fundamental rule of **Passive Voice** across all tenses is the mandatory use of the **Past Participle (V3)** form. Phrases like 'are stitch' are grammatically invalid in passive constructions.

• **Voice Definition**:

• **Passive Voice** is used when the focus is on the **action** or the **receiver** of the action (the dresses) rather than the **performer** (she).

__

• To convert a sentence from passive to active voice, the **agent** mentioned after the preposition **by** (the aviation authority) must become the **grammatical subject** of the new sentence.

• The **Present Perfect Active** voice follows the specific syntax: **Subject + has/have + V3 (Past Participle) + Object**. Since **the aviation authority** is a singular noun, the auxiliary **has** is retained.

• The **patient** or receiver of the action in the passive sentence (a new set of safety regulations) shifts to the **object** position in the active construction.

• The phrase **across all domestic airports** serves as an **adverbial adjunct** of place and remains positioned at the end of the sentence to maintain the original context and flow.

• By combining these elements, the sentence becomes: **The aviation authority** (Subject) + **has introduced** (Verb) + **a new set of safety regulations** (Object) + **across all domestic airports** (Place).

• Understanding Tense Variations:

• **Simple Past Tense:** Option 2 uses **introduced**. While it signifies a completed action, it lacks the present relevance or connection implied by the **Perfect Tense**.

• **Simple Future Tense:** Option 4 uses **will introduce**, which incorrectly shifts the timeline of the action to a future occurrence that has not yet happened.

• Voice Conversion Fundamentals:

• In **Active Voice**, the subject performs the action. It is often more **direct**, **concise**, and **authoritative** in professional writing.

• In **Passive Voice**, the subject receives the action. It is typically used when the **action** itself or the **receiver** is more important than the person or entity performing it.
